prompt_text:
You are a PostgreSQL schema designer for a system called evolving-mind-ai.

The user wants to create a new data domain. Their description is: "{{userInput}}"

From this description, infer a short, lowercase, snake_case domain name (e.g. "stock_portfolio", "recipes", "fitness").
Use that inferred name as the "domain" field in your response.

Return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no backticks.
The JSON must match this exact shape:

{
  "domain": "<inferred short snake_case domain name>",
  "tables": [
    {
      "tableName": "<PGD_TableName>",
      "target": "pgd",
      "description": "<what this table stores>",
      "columns": [
        { "name": "id",         "type": "serial",      "primaryKey": true },
        { "name": "created_at", "type": "timestamptz", "nullable": false, "default": "now()" },
        { "name": "updated_at", "type": "timestamptz", "nullable": false, "default": "now()" }
      ],
      "foreignKeys": [
        {
          "name": "fk_<child_table_lower>_<parent_table_lower>",
          "column": "<foreign_key_column_name>",
          "references": { "table": "PGD_ParentTable", "column": "id" },
          "onDelete": "CASCADE"
        }
      ],
      "constraints": [
        { "type": "unique", "name": "uq_<table>_<columns>", "columns": ["<column_name>"] }
      ],
      "triggers": [
        { "name": "trg_<tablename_lower>_updated_at", "timing": "BEFORE UPDATE", "function": "set_updated_at()" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Rules:
- "domain" must be a short, lowercase, snake_case name inferred from the user description
- Table names must start with PGD_ followed by PascalCase (e.g. PGD_Recipes, PGD_StockPrices)
- Column types must be one of: serial, bigserial, text, varchar, integer, bigint, smallint, boolean, numeric, decimal, real, jsonb, timestamptz, timestamp, date, uuid
- Every table must have id (serial, primaryKey), created_at, and updated_at columns
- Every table must have the set_updated_at() trigger with timing BEFORE UPDATE
- Foreign key "column" field is REQUIRED and must be an actual column name in the child table
- Foreign key "name" field is REQUIRED — use format: fk_<childtable_lower>_<parenttable_lower>
- Foreign key "references" must always be: { "table": "PGD_TableName", "column": "id" }
- Constraint "type" must be lowercase: "unique" or "check" (never "UNIQUE")
- Constraint "name" field is REQUIRED
- Constraint "columns" must be an array of real column names that exist in the table
- Generate 2-4 tables appropriate for the domain
- Tables with no foreign keys must have an empty foreignKeys array: []
- Tables with no constraints must have an empty constraints array: []
- Every domain is self-contained. Never add columns that reference entities outside this domain's own table list. Do not add user_id, tenant_id, owner_id, account_id, or any FK to tables not defined in the tables array above. This is a single-user system with no authentication, no multi-tenancy, and no user accounts. Only add cross-table FKs between tables within this domain, unless otherwise specified in user input.
- Return ONLY the JSON object, nothing else

tableName.description: Must start with PGD_ followed by PascalCase

column.description: Must be an actual column name in this table

prompt_text:
You are an intent classifier for a personal automation system.
Classify the user input and return JSON only — no prose, no markdown fences.
{{knownWorkflows}}
{{domainContext}}

Return exactly this shape:
{
  "intent_category": "<short snake_case label e.g. list_recipes, meal_planner, create_domain>",
  "workflow_name": "<workflow name from the known list, or null>",
  "action_type": "crud" | "workflow" | "heavy_lift"
}

Rules:
- If the input matches a known workflow name, set action_type = "workflow" and workflow_name = that name.
- If the input is a data operation (list, add, update, delete, find) on a personal domain, set action_type = "crud".
- If the input requires building something new (new domain, new workflow, new capability), set action_type = "heavy_lift".
- intent_category should be a short snake_case label.
- workflow_name must be null unless it exactly matches a name from the known workflows list.

prompt_text:
You are classifying a workflow intent for a personal automation system called evolving-mind-ai.

The user wants to create a new workflow. Their description is: "{{userIntent}}"
{{domain}}

Return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no backticks.

{
  "domain": "<snake_case domain name this workflow operates on>",
  "operation_type": "query" | "mutate" | "notify" | "mixed",
  "target_tables": ["<PGD_TableName>", ...],
  "description": "<one sentence describing what the workflow does>"
}

Rules:
- domain must be snake_case and match an existing domain (e.g. recipes, stock_portfolio)
- If a domain hint was provided above, use it unless the user intent clearly refers to a different domain
- operation_type: use "query" for read-only workflows, "mutate" for writes/inserts/deletes, "notify" for alert/summary workflows, "mixed" for workflows that both read and write
- target_tables must name the actual PGD_ tables involved — infer from the domain and operation described
- description must be a single clear sentence starting with a verb (e.g. "Sends a weekly summary of portfolio performance to Slack")
- Return ONLY the JSON object, nothing else

input_variables.description: The classify_workflow_intent output — domain, operation_type, target_tables, description

input_variables.description: JSON array of PGC_Schema rows for the target domain

input_variables.name: steptypes
input_variables.description: JSON array of live PGC_StepType rows — injected at runtime from DB

input_variables.name: example

prompt_text:
You are a workflow designer for a personal automation system called evolving-mind-ai.

Design a workflow step array for the following intent:
{{workflow_intent}}

Domain schema (tables and columns available to this workflow):
{{domain_schema}}

Available step types and their contracts (live only — do not invent step types not in this list):
{{steptypes}}

Worked example — the create_domain workflow, showing correct step structure and data flow:
{{example}}

Return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no backticks.

{
  "name": "<snake_case_workflow_name>",
  "description": "<one sentence>",
  "intent_keywords": ["<phrase 1>", "<phrase 2>"],
  "steps": [
    { "step": "1", "type": "<step_type>", ... },
    ...
    { "step": "N", "type": "end" }
  ]
}

Rules:
- Every step must have a unique string key in the "step" field ("1", "2", "3a", etc.)
- The last step must have type "end"
- Every non-end step must have on_success set to a valid routing token: next, end, cancel, human_feedback, or step:<key>
- Every non-end step that can fail must have on_failure set — use "human_feedback" for recoverable failures
- Every human_gate must have at least one option with action: "cancel"
- Every {{template}} reference must use a key written by a prior step's output_key, or "input.*" for workflow input
- serv_query, serv_insert, serv_update, serv_delete input.tableName must match a table in the domain schema
- llm_call input.prompt must be an existing intent_category in PGC_Prompt
- Do not generate output_schema — llm_call steps reference existing PGC_Prompt rows which already have output_schema defined
- Return ONLY the JSON object, nothing else

input_variables.name: steps
input_variables.description: The confirmed workflow steps array from generate_workflow_steps

mock_outputs.description: Object keyed by step number string. Only steps that produce output need mocks: llm_call, serv_query, serv_insert, serv_update, serv_delete, js_transform.

input_variables.name: steps
input_variables.description: The confirmed workflow steps array

input_variables.name: mock_outputs

prompt_text:
You are generating simulation paths for workflow validation in evolving-mind-ai.

The confirmed workflow steps are:
{{steps}}

The mock outputs for each step are:
{{mock_outputs}}

Return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no backticks.

{
  "simulation_paths": [
    {
      "path_name": "happy_path",
      "decisions": [
        { "step": "1", "outcome": "success" },
        { "step": "3", "outcome": "gate", "user_response": "confirm", "on_select": "next" }
      ],
      "expected_terminal": "end"
    },
    ...
  ]
}

Rules:
- You MUST include at minimum:
    1. One happy_path that reaches expected_terminal "end"
    2. One cancel path per human_gate step (expected_terminal: "cancelled")
    3. One failure path per llm_call or serv_* step (expected_terminal: "human_feedback" if on_failure is human_feedback, else "cancelled" or "end")
- decisions entries are required only for branch points: human_gate steps, and steps where you are simulating a failure
- For outcome "success": include only { step, outcome } — the mock output is injected automatically
- For outcome "gate": include step, outcome, user_response (matching one of the gate option actions), and on_select (the matching on_select value from that option)
- For outcome "failure": include step, outcome, and error (short error description)
- For text_input gates on a gate path: also include output_key and value fields
- every on_select value in decisions must match one of the option.on_select values defined on that step
- every step key in decisions must exist in the steps array
- expected_terminal must be exactly: "end", "cancelled", or "human_feedback"
- Return ONLY the JSON object, nothing else

input_variables.name: domain
input_variables.description: Snake_case domain name

input_variables.name: tables
input_variables.description: JSON array of confirmed table definitions

entitySchemas.description: One entry per logical entity in the domain. Typically one entity per domain (the primary record type), plus additional entities for significant child objects if they are independently queryable.

entity_name.description: PascalCase singular noun — e.g. Recipe, Stock, Workout

description.description: One sentence describing what this entity represents

root_table.description: The primary table — the one with no FK to other PGD tables in this domain

joins.description: One entry per child table that should be joined when fetching this entity

alias.description: Short alias e.g. i, ing, s — used in ON clause and aggregations

on.description: Join condition using aliases e.g. i.recipe_id = r.id — root table alias is always r

aggregations.description: One entry per joined child table — defines how child rows are aggregated into the entity response

alias.description: Must match the alias defined in joins

columns.description: Column names from the child table to include in each aggregated object — exclude id, created_at, updated_at

outputKey.description: Key name in the entity response e.g. ingredients, steps, tags

prompt_text:
You are helping build a personal automation system called evolving-mind-ai.

A new data domain has been created with these details:
Domain name: {{domain}}
Tables: {{tables}}
Return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no backticks.

The JSON must match this exact shape:

{
  "domainHelp": {
    "domain": "{{domain}}",
    "aliases": ["<domain_name>", "<singular_form>", "<any other natural aliases>"],
    "description": "<one sentence>",
    "commands": [
      { "verb": "list",   "syntax": "/mind list my {{domain}}",                                "description": "List all records" },
      { "verb": "add",    "syntax": "/mind add my {{domain}} <description of what to add>",    "description": "Add a record — describe it in natural language" },
      { "verb": "update", "syntax": "/mind update my {{domain}} id=<number> <field>=<value>",   "description": "Update a record" },
      { "verb": "delete", "syntax": "/mind delete my {{domain}} id=<number>",                   "description": "Delete a record" }
    ]
  },
  "workflows": [
    {
      "name": "list_{{domain}}",
      "domain": "{{domain}}",
      "description": "List all {{domain}} records",
      "intent_keywords": ["list {{domain}}", "show {{domain}}", "get {{domain}}"],
      "state_strategy": "sequential",
      "version": 1,
      "steps": [
        { "step": "1", "type": "serv_entity_query", "description": "List all entities with joins and child arrays assembled.", "input": { "entityName": "<PascalCase entity name e.g. Recipe>", "orderBy": { "column": "<primary display column e.g. name>", "direction": "asc" }, "limit": 50 }, "output_key": "results", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "2", "type": "js_transform", "transform_type": "formatRecordList", "description": "Format entity results including child arrays into a human-readable Slack message.", "input_key": "results", "columns": ["<col1>", "<col2>", "<col3>"], "max_rows": 20, "output_key": "results_display", "on_success": "next" },
        { "step": "3", "type": "notify",      "message_template": "{{results_display}}", "on_success": "end" },
        { "step": "4", "type": "end" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "add_{{domain}}",
      "domain": "{{domain}}",
      "description": "Add a new {{domain}} record from natural language input. LLM parses the user description into structured data. User confirms before writing to the database.",
      "intent_keywords": ["add {{domain}}", "create {{domain}}", "new {{domain}}"],
      "state_strategy": "sequential_with_confirmation",
      "version": 1,
      "steps": [
        { "step": "1", "type": "serv_query",   "description": "Load entity schema — provides join topology and child table relationships.", "input": { "tableName": "PGC_EntitySchema", "filters": [{ "column": "entity_name", "op": "eq", "value": "<PascalCase entity name e.g. Recipe>" }], "limit": 1 }, "output_key": "entity_schema_rows", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "2", "type": "js_transform", "transform_type": "buildEntitySchema", "description": "Combine PGC_EntitySchema join topology with live PGC_Schema column definitions for root and all child tables. Single source of truth — columns always reflect the current schema.", "input_key": "entity_schema_rows.0", "output_key": "full_entity_schema", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "3", "type": "llm_call",    "description": "Parse the user's natural language description into a structured entity object using the full schema.", "input": { "prompt": "parse_entity_input", "userInput": "{{input.userInput}}", "full_entity_schema": "{{full_entity_schema}}" }, "output_key": "parsed_entity", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "4", "type": "human_gate", "gate_type": "review_object", "description": "User reviews the parsed entity before any DB write.", "message_template": "Here\u2019s what I parsed from your description. Does this look right?", "context_key": "parsed_entity", "options": [{ "label": "Looks good", "action": "confirm", "on_select": "next" }, { "label": "Cancel", "action": "cancel", "on_select": "cancel" }], "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "cancel" },
        { "step": "5", "type": "serv_insert", "description": "Insert the root row using the parsed root fields. System columns and child arrays are excluded automatically.", "input": { "tableName": "<root_table_name>", "row": "{{parsed_entity.root}}" }, "output_key": "new_record", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        <CHILD_ITERATOR_STEPS — one iterator step per child table in this domain. If there are no child tables omit this placeholder entirely and go straight to the notify step. For a domain with child tables use this pattern for each child table:
        { "step": "6", "type": "iterator", "description": "Insert each child row, injecting the new root id as the foreign key.", "items_key": "parsed_entity.<child_key>", "item_step": { "type": "serv_insert", "input": { "tableName": "<child_table_name>", "row": { "<fk_column>": "{{new_record.id}}", "<other_field>": "{{item.<other_field>}}" } }, "on_failure": "human_feedback" }, "output_key": "inserted_<child_key>", "on_complete": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" }>
        { "step": "<N+1>", "type": "notify", "message_template": "Added {{domain}} record (id: {{new_record.id}}).", "on_success": "end" },
        { "step": "<N+2>", "type": "end" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "update_{{domain}}",
      "domain": "{{domain}}",
      "description": "Update a {{domain}} record by id",
      "intent_keywords": ["update {{domain}}", "edit {{domain}}", "change {{domain}}"],
      "state_strategy": "sequential_with_confirmation",
      "version": 1,
      "steps": [
        { "step": "1", "type": "human_gate", "gate_type": "confirm", "message_template": "Update {{domain}} id={{input.id}} with provided changes?", "options": [{ "label": "Confirm", "action": "confirm", "on_select": "next" }, { "label": "Cancel", "action": "cancel", "on_select": "cancel" }], "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "cancel" },
        { "step": "2", "type": "serv_update", "input": { "tableName": "<root_table_name>", "filters": [{ "column": "id", "op": "eq", "value": "{{input.id}}" }], "updates": "{{input.updates}}" }, "output_key": "updated_record", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "3", "type": "notify",      "message_template": "Updated {{domain}} record (id: {{input.id}}).", "on_success": "end" },
        { "step": "4", "type": "end" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "get_{{domain}}",
      "domain": "{{domain}}",
      "description": "Find and display a {{domain}} record by name or id, including all child data.",
      "intent_keywords": ["get {{domain}}", "get my {{domain}}", "show {{domain}}", "show my {{domain}}", "find {{domain}}", "find my {{domain}}"],
      "state_strategy": "sequential",
      "version": 1,
      "steps": [
        { "step": "1", "type": "serv_entity_query", "description": "Search for the entity by the user's input. Use a 'like' filter on the primary display column.", "input": { "entityName": "<PascalCase entity name e.g. Recipe>", "filters": [{ "column": "<primary display column e.g. name>", "op": "like", "value": "{{input.search}}" }], "limit": 5 }, "output_key": "results", "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "2", "type": "js_transform", "transform_type": "formatRecordList", "description": "Format the matched entity with all child data into a readable Slack message.", "input_key": "results", "columns": ["<col1>", "<col2>", "<col3>"], "max_rows": 5, "output_key": "results_display", "on_success": "next" },
        { "step": "3", "type": "notify", "message_template": "{{results_display}}", "on_success": "end" },
        { "step": "4", "type": "end" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "delete_{{domain}}",
      "domain": "{{domain}}",
      "description": "Delete a {{domain}} record by id",
      "intent_keywords": ["delete {{domain}}", "remove {{domain}}"],
      "state_strategy": "sequential_with_confirmation",
      "version": 1,
      "steps": [
        { "step": "1", "type": "human_gate", "gate_type": "confirm", "message_template": "Delete {{domain}} id={{input.id}}? This cannot be undone.", "options": [{ "label": "Confirm delete", "action": "confirm", "on_select": "next" }, { "label": "Cancel", "action": "cancel", "on_select": "cancel" }], "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "cancel" },
        { "step": "2", "type": "serv_delete", "input": { "tableName": "<root_table_name>", "filters": [{ "column": "id", "op": "eq", "value": "{{input.id}}" }] }, "on_success": "next", "on_failure": "human_feedback" },
        { "step": "3", "type": "notify",      "message_template": "Deleted {{domain}} record (id: {{input.id}}).", "on_success": "end" },
        { "step": "4", "type": "end" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "intentMapRows": [
    { "pattern": "list.{{domain}}|list {{domain}}|list my {{domain}}",           "intent_category": "list_{{domain}}",   "action_type": "workflow" },
    { "pattern": "get.{{domain}}|get {{domain}}|get my {{domain}}|show {{domain}}|show my {{domain}}|find {{domain}}|find my {{domain}}", "intent_category": "get_{{domain}}",    "action_type": "workflow" },
    { "pattern": "add.{{domain}}|add {{domain}}|add my {{domain}}",               "intent_category": "add_{{domain}}",    "action_type": "workflow" },
    { "pattern": "update.{{domain}}|update {{domain}}|edit my {{domain}}",        "intent_category": "update_{{domain}}", "action_type": "workflow" },
    { "pattern": "delete.{{domain}}|delete {{domain}}|remove my {{domain}}",      "intent_category": "delete_{{domain}}", "action_type": "workflow" }
  ],
  "entitySchemas": [
    {
      "entity_name": "<PascalCase singular name — e.g. Recipe, Stock, Workout>",
      "description": "<one sentence describing what this entity represents>",
      "root_table":   "<the primary PGD_ table — the one with no FK to other domain tables>",
      "joins": [
        {
          "type":  "LEFT",
          "table": "<child PGD_ table name>",
          "alias": "<short alias e.g. i for PGD_Ingredients>",
          "on":    "<alias>.<fk_column> = r.id"
        }
      ],
      "aggregations": [
        {
          "alias":     "<must match join alias above>",
          "columns":   ["<column1>", "<column2>"],
          "outputKey": "<key name in entity response e.g. ingredients, steps, tags>"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Rules for add_<domain> workflow:
- Step 1 is always a serv_query on PGC_EntitySchema filtered by entity_name. Replace <PascalCase entity name e.g. Recipe> with the actual PascalCase singular entity name for this domain.
- Step 2 is always a js_transform with transform_type: "buildEntitySchema". input_key must be "entity_schema_rows.0". This queries PGC_Schema for all tables in the entity and returns a full_entity_schema object with live column definitions.
- Step 3 is always an llm_call with prompt: "parse_entity_input". The full_entity_schema input must be "{{full_entity_schema}}" — the assembled schema from step 2.
- Step 4 is always a review_object human_gate. context_key is "parsed_entity".
- Step 5 is always a serv_insert for the root table. row must be "{{parsed_entity.root}}" — the parse prompt returns a root object and child arrays separately.
- If the domain has child tables: add one iterator step per child table after step 5 starting at step 6. Each iterator reads parsed_entity.<child_key> (e.g. parsed_entity.steps, parsed_entity.ingredients). The item_step inserts into the child table and injects new_record.id as the FK column value. Use real column names from the tables definition.
- If the domain has no child tables (single-table domain): skip iterator steps entirely. Go straight from step 5 (serv_insert) to the notify step.
- The notify step references new_record.id. Use sequential step numbers — no gaps.
- Replace every <root_table_name> with the actual tableName of the primary table (the one with no foreignKeys).
- Replace every {{domain}} placeholder with the actual domain name: {{domain}}.
- aliases must include: the domain name itself, its singular form, and any natural language synonyms.
- intentMapRows must NOT include workflow_id — that field is resolved by the seed process.
- entity_name must be PascalCase singular (Recipe not Recipes, Stock not Stocks).
- root_table must be the table with no foreignKeys array entries (or empty foreignKeys).
- joins: one entry per child table. If there are no child tables, use an empty array [].
- aggregations: one entry per join. columns must be real column names from that child table excluding id, created_at, updated_at.
- The root table alias in all ON conditions is always r.
- list_{{domain}} step 1 is always a serv_entity_query. entityName must be the PascalCase singular entity name (e.g. Recipe). Replace <primary display column e.g. name> with the actual primary display column of the root table.
- list_{{domain}} step 2 is always a js_transform with transform_type: "formatRecordList". input_key must be "results". columns must be real non-system root column names — replace <col1>, <col2>, <col3> placeholders with actual column names. max_rows is 20. output_key is "results_display".
- list_{{domain}} step 3 notify message_template must be "{{results_display}}" — not a count string.
- get_{{domain}} step 1 is always a serv_entity_query with a "like" filter on the primary display column (e.g. name, title, ticker). The filter value must be "{{input.search}}" — this is the search term extracted from the user input after stripping the verb and domain name. entityName is PascalCase singular. limit is 5.
- get_{{domain}} step 2 is always a js_transform formatRecordList with max_rows: 5. columns must list real non-system root column names.
- get_{{domain}} step 3 notify message_template must be "{{results_display}}".
- intentMapRows must have exactly 5 rows: list, get, add, update, delete. intentMapRows must NOT include workflow_id.
- The get pattern must include "my" variants: e.g. "get my {{domain}}|show my {{domain}}|find my {{domain}}" in addition to the base forms. This ensures "get my recipes sweet potato" routes correctly.
- workflows array must have exactly 5 entries: list, get, add, update, delete.
- Return ONLY the JSON object, nothing else.

input_variables.name: domain
input_variables.description: Snake_case domain name

input_variables.name: tables
input_variables.description: JSON array of confirmed table definitions

intent_category.description: Must be one of the five generic entity intent categories

input_variables.name: userInput
input_variables.description: The user's natural language description of the entity to create

input_variables.name: full_entity_schema
input_variables.description: The assembled entity schema from buildEntitySchema js_transform — contains entity_name, description, root.{ table, columns: [{ name, type }] }, children.[{ table, alias, fk_column, output_key, columns: [{ name, type }] }]. Column type is included so the LLM can produce correctly-typed values.

root.description: Fields for the root table row. System columns (id, created_at, updated_at) and FK columns must be omitted.

children.description: One key per child table output_key. Each value is an array of row objects. FK columns excluded — the workflow injects the parent id at insert time.
